purpose: Resolve Phase 1 Real Estate sector benchmark policy on data-integrity grounds before freezing the Phase 1 dataset spec. No IC, decile, or signal-performance metric was computed.
phase_0F_frozen_spec_reference: frozen hypothesis names 'SPDR sector ETF' as the β=1 sector benchmark; XLRE was the intended Real Estate benchmark

option_analyses.label: use XLRE from a compatible external source

candidate_sources_reviewed.verdict: same IEX-only regime as HF post-2022; would still leave pre-2016 gap; introduces third feed source with unclear adjustment/timestamp semantics
would work but is paid; unknown alignment with HF's pitrading/iex composite; corporate-action policy differs; no way to verify bar-boundary convention matches HF
high quality but paid, and cross-source risk remains

data_integrity_concerns: Splices a 3rd source into the dataset — timestamp convention (bar start vs bar end), holiday handling, corporate-action treatment, and last-print policy may differ from HF.
Pre-XLRE-inception (before 2015-10-08) still leaves Real Estate without a sector benchmark; Option A does NOT solve pre-2015 windows.
Verification of alignment requires per-bar comparison against HF on overlapping periods — non-trivial and cannot fully rule out subtle discrepancies.
Free reliable source for 5m XLRE 2015-2022 does not exist per web search (2026-09-28).
option_analyses.spec_impact: preserves frozen hypothesis spec exactly (post-2015-10-08 only)

option_analyses.label: exclude Real Estate constituents
data_integrity_concerns: None — 100% internal to HF dataset; no external splice; no timestamp/adjustment ambiguity.
option_analyses.spec_impact: hypothesis spec applies to 10 of 11 sectors (all sectors except Real Estate); explicitly documented scope narrowing rather than spec change; cross-sectional signal at 13:00 ET evaluated on ~476 tickers per session instead of ~502
additional_notes: XLRE launched 2015-10-08 — pre-2015 RE stocks classified as Financials in GICS anyway; Option B removes an ambiguity across the GICS 2016 carve-out.
Reduced cross-section increases per-timestamp IC standard error by roughly sqrt(502/476) ≈ 1.027, i.e. ~2.7% larger — negligible for statistical power.

option_analyses.label: use IYR as an explicitly documented specification deviation

coverage_impact.note: Preserves all Real Estate stocks in cross-section (0% loss)

option_analyses.spec_impact: SIGNIFICANT — sector-relative representation for Real Estate stocks becomes 'stock minus IYR' instead of 'stock minus XLRE'. IYR tracks the Dow Jones U.S. Real Estate Capped Index (~85 constituents including mid/small-cap REITs, mortgage REITs, and real estate services), a different universe from XLRE's ~30 S&P 500 REITs. The typical XLRE/IYR daily-return correlation is ~0.95-0.98 (high but not identical); residuals from the two benchmarks are not interchangeable at the 5-minute cross-sectional level.
data_integrity_concerns: None on the data-integrity axis (same HF source, deep history 2003+).

BUT: this is a *specification deviation*. The frozen Phase 0F hypothesis names 'SPDR sector ETF' as the β=1 sector benchmark. Substituting IYR is a rewrite of that clause, not a mere technical fill-in.
additional_notes: If C is chosen, Phase 2 confirmation is testing a DIFFERENT frozen spec than what was preregistered.
Recording IYR-based Phase 2 results as confirmation of the Phase 0F hypothesis would be misleading.

recommendation.label: exclude Real Estate constituents
recommendation.rationale: Purely on data-integrity grounds: Option B is the only choice that introduces no external data (Option A) and no specification deviation (Option C). The coverage impact is small — 3.07% of the PIT universe in the trustworthy window (2001+), 3.84% in the best HF-coverage window (2011-2022), and ~5.8% in the modern post-2022 regime. Statistical power loss is negligible (~2.7% larger per-timestamp IC standard error). The frozen Phase 0F hypothesis remains applied exactly as written to 10 of 11 sectors; the exclusion is a documented scope narrowing, not a spec change.
recommendation.operational_rule: Filter out any (ticker, session) row where sector_map[ticker] == 'XLRE'. Applied at the eligibility layer inside phase1.eligibility before the cross-sectional ranking step. Never derive Real Estate sector-relative returns; those stocks are simply absent from Phase 2 cross-sections.
consequences_documented_for_phase_2: Cross-section size at each decision time drops by ~26-29 names post-2016.
Real Estate-specific reversal (if any) will not be evaluated by Phase 2. This is a scope limitation acknowledged upfront, not a survivorship issue.
If a future Phase 10 research cycle wants to test Real Estate reversal, that requires an independent XLRE data source and a NEW preregistered hypothesis.
